title: Interval DP
tagline: Solve a range by trying every split point — DP over subintervals [l, r].

intuition.analogy: Deciding the cheapest way to chain-multiply a row of matrices: you pick where to make the final 'cut', solve each side optimally, and pay for combining them. You try every possible cut and keep the cheapest.
paragraphs: Interval DP solves problems on a contiguous range [l, r] by choosing a split (or a last action) inside the range and combining the optimal solutions of the resulting subranges.
The state dp[l][r] represents the best answer for the subarray from l to r. The transition tries every k between l and r: dp[l][r] = best over k of dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + cost(l, k, r).
You fill by increasing interval length so that all smaller subintervals are ready. It models matrix-chain multiplication, optimal BSTs, burst balloons, and merging-stones-style problems.
intuition.keyIdea: dp[l][r] combines dp[l][k] and dp[k+1][r] over all split points k; iterate by increasing length.

steps.title: Base case
steps.detail: Single elements (l == r) usually cost 0 or a trivial value.

steps.title: Increase interval length
steps.detail: For len from 2 to n, for each l, set r = l + len − 1.

steps.title: Try every split
steps.detail: dp[l][r] = optimum over k in [l, r) of dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + merge-cost. Sometimes the 'last' element to act is chosen instead of a split (e.g. burst balloons).

codes.source:
def matrix_chain(p):              # p[0..n]; matrix i has dims p[i-1] x p[i]
    n = len(p) - 1
    INF = float('inf')
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for length in range(2, n + 1):
        for l in range(1, n - length + 2):
            r = l + length - 1
            dp[l][r] = INF
            for k in range(l, r):
                dp[l][r] = min(dp[l][r],
                               dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r] + p[l-1]*p[k]*p[r])
    return dp[1][n]

complexity.timeReason: n² intervals, each trying up to n split points.
complexity.spaceReason: The dp table over interval endpoints.

pitfalls: Fill by increasing length, not by raw l/r loops, or dependencies won't be ready.
Some problems pick a 'last action' (burst balloons) rather than a clean split — identify which.
Add sentinels at the boundaries when the merge cost references neighbours outside [l, r].

dryRun.clickMoment: Choosing which balloon bursts LAST in a range fixes its neighbours as the range's borders — turning a messy global order into clean independent subintervals.

problems.title: Burst Balloons
problems.hint: Pick the last balloon to burst in each interval.

approach: Think of the LAST balloon to burst in an interval (i, j). When it bursts, its neighbours are exactly the boundaries i and j (everything inside is gone).
dp[i][j] = max coins bursting all balloons strictly between i and j. Try each k as the last: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][k] + a[i]·a[k]·a[j] + dp[k][j]). Pad the array with 1s on both ends.

problems.title: Matrix Chain (Min Score Triangulation)
problems.statement: Min triangulation score of a polygon.
problems.hint: dp[l][r] over the apex vertex k.

approach: Triangulating a polygon: pick the third vertex k of the triangle on edge (i, j). That splits the polygon into two sub-polygons.
dp[i][j] = min over k of dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + v[i]·v[k]·v[j]. Base: adjacent vertices cost 0.

problems.title: Stone Game / Merge Stones
problems.statement: Minimum cost to merge stone piles.
problems.hint: Interval DP with a merge-cost (prefix sums).

approach: Both players play optimally, so track the score difference (current player minus opponent) on each interval.
dp[i][j] = max(take left: a[i] - dp[i+1][j], take right: a[j] - dp[i][j-1]). The first player wins iff dp over the whole array is positive.

problems.title: Strange Printer
problems.statement: Min turns to print a string.

approach: dp[i][j] = minimum turns to print s[i..j]. Printing s[i] can also cover a later equal character, merging the work.
Start with dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j] + 1 (print s[i] alone). For any k in (i, j] with s[k]==s[i], combine: dp[i][j] = min(dp[i][j], dp[i+1][k-1] + dp[k][j]).

problems.title: Palindrome Partitioning II
problems.statement: Min cuts to partition into palindromes.
problems.hint: Precompute palindrome ranges, then interval/linear DP.

approach: Precompute pal[i][j] = whether s[i..j] is a palindrome using interval DP (it is iff ends match and the inside is a palindrome).
Then cut[i] = min cuts for s[0..i]: if s[0..i] is a palindrome, 0; else min over j of cut[j-1]+1 where s[j..i] is a palindrome.
